    Case study 03 · Governed agents

    In preparation for release

    WAGF

    A Water Agent Governance Framework that checks proposed LLM-agent decisions before they update a human–water simulation.

    • structured decision contract
    • physical + financial + behavioral checks
    • deterministic audit trace

    Problem

    Why this problem matters

    A syntactically valid action can still violate physical limits, household finances, behavioral theory, or the current simulation state.

    For AI teams

    The governance pattern transfers to any stateful agent system where an action must satisfy explicit constraints and leave an audit trail before execution.

    Evidence slice

    From question to consequence

    Public statusFramework in preparation. The trace below is synthetic and illustrative.

    01Problem
    An unconstrained LLM proposal can create impossible financial or physical state changes.
    02My role
    I designed the proposal schema, validator sequence, targeted repair path, and audit record.
    03Input
    A synthetic household state, action catalog, and explicit behavioral, financial, and physical constraints.
    04Decision
    The model proposes an action with typed parameters but cannot write to state.
    05Validation
    A failed affordability check blocks the update; repair changes only the invalid field before all validators rerun.
    06Consequence
    The accepted proposal is committed with a trace linking input, failure, repair, and final state update.

    3. LLM proposal

      Repeated model runs produce a choice and a concise rationale for comparison.

      Checks compare direction, subgroup behavior, and run-to-run stability without exposing respondent records.

      The result becomes an evaluation finding, not a claim that the model represents a person.

    Research context and method

    Frozen demonstration · no live model call

    1. Proposed action
    2. Parser
    3. Physical check
    4. Financial check
    5. Behavioral check
    6. Audit record
    7. State update
    Blocked

    Rejected: cost exceeds available household budget

    Role & method

    What I built

    I designed the context builder, structured decision schema, parser, validators, targeted repair loop, audit record, and simulation-state boundary.

    1. Build context from approved persona and simulation state.
    2. Require a structured action and ratings.
    3. Parse before any state mutation.
    4. Run physical, financial, and behavioral-theory checks.
    5. Accept, reject, or request targeted repair.
    6. Write the trace, then update state only for an accepted action.

    Validation and limitations

    Validation

    • Schema validation
    • Fail-closed parser boundary
    • Named rule results
    • Deterministic demonstration trace
    • State update occurs after acceptance

    Limitations

    • Declared rules cannot cover every failure mode.
    • Repair can satisfy a rule while still producing a weak decision.
    • The framework remains in preparation for release.
    • Demonstration records are illustrative, not research outcomes.

    What changed

    Governance is clearest when every decision exposes the proposal, the rule that failed, the allowed repair, and the exact state transition.
